 Follow Us On: News India Cyclone Akvan forms over Bay of Bengal, likely to hit Andhra coast on November 20 Cyclone Akvan forms over Bay of Bengal, likely to hit Andhra coast on November 20
 Cyclone Akvan is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on November 20, with gusts of up to 145 kmph at landfall. Heavy rain is forecast in parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Tamil Nadu.
 Advertisement The IMD has issued an orange cyclone alert for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts. (File photo-AP) By : Ajay Nath , Pramod Madhav New Delhi , Nov 17, 2026 07:12 IST Last Updated Nov 17, 2026 07:12 IST Published by Aprameya Rao Nov 16, 2026 23:36 IST Edited by Aprameya Rao The deep depression over the Bay of Bengal intensified into Cyclone Akvan on Monday evening. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the storm was likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on November 20 as a very severe cyclonic storm.
 The IMD has issued an orange cyclone alert for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts. It expects sustained winds of 120–130 kmph, with gusts of up to 145 kmph, at landfall.
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Heavy to very heavy rain is likely in parts of coastal Andhra Pradesh on November 19 and 20, with extremely heavy rain possible at isolated locations. In Odisha, the weather department has forecast heavy to very heavy rain from November 19 to 21.
 At 5.30 pm IST on Monday, Akvan was about 660 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 670 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 790 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha.
 ANDHRA PREPARES FOR 3RD CYCLONE IN THREE WEEKS
 Andhra Pradesh is bracing for its third cyclone in three weeks . Cyclone Akvan is expected to cross the coast on November 20, after cyclones Arnab and Murasu damaged crops across the state and caused losses that the government estimated at nearly Rs 7,000 crore.
 Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to deploy national and state disaster response teams ahead of landfall and keep electricity crews ready to restore power in case of outages.
 Officials identified Konaseema, Kakinada, East Godavari, West Godavari, Krishna, NTR and Guntur as districts likely to be affected. The IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rain in parts of coastal Andhra Pradesh on November 19 and 20, with extremely heavy rain possible at isolated locations. HEAVY RAIN LIKELY IN ODISHA FROM NOVEMBER 18
 Cyclone Akvan is likely to bring heavy rain to parts of Odisha from November 18. The IMD has issued a yellow alert for 16 districts that day and forecast heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places from November 19 to 21. Strong winds are also likely in parts of the state during this period.
 Puri, Ganjam and Gajapati are under an orange alert for November 19. The alert covers Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri on November 20. On November 21, it covers the western districts of Bargarh, Jharsuguda and Sundargarh.
 The Odisha government has asked officials in southern districts to move people to safety before heavy rain begins. In Ganjam, officials have identified low-lying areas that could flood and hill settlements at risk of landslides. At least 10 people were killed in landslides in Ganjam and Kandhamal during Cyclone Arnab . HEAVY RAIN LIKELY IN NORTHERN TAMIL NADU
 advertisement The IMD has forecast heavy rain at isolated places in northern Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on November 17 and 20, and heavy to very heavy rain on November 18 and 19.
 Seas off northern Tamil Nadu and Puducherry are expected to remain rough to very rough until November 20. Fishermen have been advised to stay out of the southwest and west-central Bay of Bengal until then. Winds along and off the coast could gust to 70 kmph on November 19 and 20.
 Earlier this month, Cyclone Murasu brought heavy rain to northern Tamil Nadu as it approached the Andhra Pradesh coast. Several roads in Chennai were waterlogged on November 2, schools closed for the day and some flights were cancelled. - Ends
